tiles.title: The first clearing
tiles.description: A tiny observatory rises from a lush garden island encircled by a spiral river, with golden paths threading among impossible plants.
tiles.continuity: Continue meticulous dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and translucent watercolor on warm parchment; midnight teal water, verdigris vegetation, ochre golden paths, restrained coral plants. Founding center has a miniature teal-domed stone observatory with brass telescope, one anonymous tiny walker, cypress silhouettes, branching fantastical plants and a flowing open spiral river. Narrow gold paths leave near the midpoint of north, east, south and west edges; water, mossy stone, low garden terrain and botanical detail fill every edge. Grow the landscape outside those exits without duplicating the observatory, closing off paths or changing the established scale.

tiles.title: The Rootglass Orchard
tiles.description: Translucent mineral trees rise among mossy garden terraces beneath a root arch carrying water into a lily-filled stream.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square east of the founding clearing. Warm parchment, meticulous dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor, midnight teal water, restrained coral shrubs; same high bird's-eye/isometric miniature scale. A gold path enters the left edge at about 45 percent height, crosses a small stone arch bridge and threads terraced mossy stone gardens. Pale faceted glasslike fern trees occupy stepped central and upper terraces. A great root arch in the upper-right carries a narrow teal watercourse and a waterfall into lily pools below. Cypress silhouettes, fine flowers, stone steps, mineral outcrops and branching waterways fill the edges. Golden paths remain open at the top, lower center and right edge near 90 percent height; narrow teal waterways run through the right and lower portions. Continue these terrain and botanical details across adjoining edges without repeating the orchard's principal root arch or the original observatory.

tiles.title: The Ammonite Mere
tiles.description: A great moss-covered limestone spiral cradles a lily basin among cascading reed wetlands and winding golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square directly south of Rootglass Orchard. Warm parchment, meticulous dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor with midnight teal water and restrained coral flowers; coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature scale. The upper edge continues a gold path near midpoint, a narrow teal stream near one-third width and a teal channel at the far right among rocky terraces, cypresses and pale faceted fern trees. A giant curled limestone shell occupies the center, its mossy ribbed whorl enclosing a teal lily basin with a small coiled stone at the heart. Cascades, lily pads, tall reeds and white iris-like flowers fill surrounding wetlands. Golden paths cross small stone arch bridges at left-middle and lower-right, with paths exiting left near one-third and four-fifths height, at the bottom near two-fifths width, and right near four-fifths height. Teal channels remain open at the lower center and bottom-right. Continue wetland water, rocky banks and path connections; do not repeat the central stone shell or earlier landmarks.

tiles.title: The Droplet Willow
tiles.description: A willow bears translucent water-filled seedpods that drip into a terraced marsh crossed by golden paths and small stone bridges.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (0,1), south of The first clearing and west of The Ammonite Mere. Meticulous dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight teal water and restrained coral flowers; coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature scale. A gnarled willow dominates center-left, its long hanging leaves framing clear pear-shaped pods of teal water that drip into circular ripples. Rocky wetland terraces, little waterfalls, cypresses, pale faceted fern-like plants, reeds, white irises and lily pads surround it. Two stone arch footbridges cross channels at left-middle and lower-right-middle. Top edge has golden paths near midpoint and upper-left, teal streams around one-third and three-quarters width. Gold trails reach left near halfway height, right near halfway and four-fifths height, and bottom near two-fifths width. Water remains open at the bottom center-right and along the left marsh edge. Continue rocky banks, wetland channels and gold trails; introduce a fresh discovery rather than repeating this willow, the shell or observatory.

tiles.title: The Levity Wells
tiles.description: A hovering limestone lily pool spills fine waterfalls into a smaller well amid terraced wetlands and golden stairways.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-1,1), west of The Droplet Willow. Detailed dark ink, fine crosshatching and translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight teal water, sparse coral flowers; coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature scale. Center-left holds a large circular limestone basin of lily pads and pale pink water lilies, hovering above a smaller rocky well; thin waterfalls cross the visible air gap into rippling teal water. Cream craggy terraces, reed beds, white irises, slim cypresses and pale faceted leaves surround winding channels, gold paths and several stone stairs. A modest arch bridge at right-middle carries a gold path toward the eastern neighbor; hanging willow branches with droplets enter from the right edge. Golden paths reach the left edge near the upper margin, halfway height and lower quarter, the top in the right half, the right near halfway height, and the bottom in the right half. Teal water remains open at top near two-fifths width, bottom across the central area and lower-left corner, and right across middle and lower wetland edges. Continue these rocky wetland terraces, gold trails and teal channels; the next northern region should connect to the upper streams and paths while introducing a fresh discovery.

tiles.title: The Tide Harp
tiles.description: A limestone crescent pours delicate water strings into a terraced lily stream amid cypresses and golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-1,0), north of The Levity Wells and west of The first clearing. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight teal water, restrained coral flowers; coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. A tall pale limestone crescent in the upper-left center carries multiple fine vertical water strings from its curved upper rib into a teal pool. Rough cream stone terraces, small waterfalls, lily pads and pale pink lilies, white irises, reeds, slim dark cypresses, pale faceted leaves and a coral flowering tree surround branching waterways. Golden paths wind over short stone stairs, with a low arch bridge at right-middle. Bottom water stays open around the central-left area toward the southern wells, and a gold trail reaches the bottom in the right half. The right edge has a gold path near halfway height connecting to the founding clearing, with rocky planted terrain and wetland channels above it. A gold trail leaves the top near the middle and teal water leaves the top in the left half; gold trails also reach the left around halfway height and the lower quarter. Continue the water, rocky garden terraces and golden trails into a new discovery, keeping this limestone water harp unique.

tiles.title: The Rainseed Orchard
tiles.description: A twisting tree rises from a split stone seed, its shallow water-bowl leaves spilling fine streams into terraced garden pools.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-1,-1), directly north of The Tide Harp. Detailed dark ink contours and fine crosshatching with translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; midnight teal water, restrained coral blossoms, and the same high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Left of center, one twisting dark tree grows from two cracked pale ochre stone seed-shell halves; its crown is formed by shallow green bowls of teal water, with fine falling streams feeding the root pool and a waterfall through the split shell. Rough cream limestone terraces, small cascades, lily pads and pale pink lilies, white irises, reeds, slim dark cypresses, pale faceted leaves, and coral and white flowering trees surround the branching channels. A low arched stone footbridge stands at right-middle with shallow steps on both approaches. The bottom river reaches the edge in the left third and the golden trail near the middle, adjoining the southern tile's northern river and trail. A curved pale stone rib is clipped by the bottom edge near center-left. Teal water remains open at the top around the left quarter and at the right edge around the upper third. A golden trail reaches the top in the right half and the right edge just below halfway height; another golden trail reaches the left around the lower-middle. Continue the rocky planted terraces, teal channels, and readable golden paths while keeping this water-bowl tree unique.

tiles.title: The Suspended Ford
tiles.description: Hovering limestone stepping stones drip into a teal pool between flowering terraces and winding golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (0,-1), east of The Rainseed Orchard and north of The first clearing. Detailed dark ink contours and fine hatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water and restrained coral blossoms at the established high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. A diagonal line of broad flat pale limestone stepping stones crosses the central pool from lower-left toward upper-right; the stones hover above the water with thin falling threads and ripples beneath them. Cream rocky terraces, multiple small cascades, lily pads and pale pink lilies, white irises, reeds, slim dark cypresses, large pale faceted leaves, and coral and white flowering trees fill the banks. A freestanding weathered stone arch stands in the upper-right garden beside shallow path steps. The golden trail enters the left edge just below halfway and leads toward the ford; it also reaches the bottom near the middle, adjoining the southern clearing's northern trail. Teal water reaches the left edge around the upper third and the top across the left-middle; planted limestone ledges connect the western orchard border. A golden trail exits the top in the right half and reaches the right edge around the upper-middle. Teal channels remain open along the right side at upper and middle heights, and near the bottom around the right three-quarters. A pale curved stone rib is clipped by the bottom left of center. Continue the teal channels, readable golden paths, planted limestone terraces, medium, scale and soft upper-left light while keeping this hovering ford unique.

tiles.title: The Petalwell Garden
tiles.description: A pale limestone flower cradles teal pools in its open petals, spilling cascades into a terraced lily garden.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (1,-1), east of The Suspended Ford and north of The Rootglass Orchard. Detailed dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water and coral flowers at the established high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale, with soft upper-left light. A large pale limestone flower occupies the upper-right center: tall curved stone petals surround shallow teal petal pools at several heights, and narrow white waterfalls descend into lily pools beneath. Cream blocky limestone terraces, slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, small yellow and white flowers, coral flowering shrubs and trees, pale faceted leaves and a cream flowering tree in the lower middle fill the banks. Golden paths enter the left edge in the upper fifth, wind through shallow steps and terraces, pass across the lower middle and exit the bottom in the right-middle. Golden trails also reach the top near the left-middle and right-middle, and the right edge in the upper quarter. Teal channels are open at the top near the left quarter, along multiple parts of the left edge, the right edge at middle and lower heights, and the bottom at left and middle heights. Planted limestone ledges, gold trails and teal water continue the western and southern garden boundaries; a cropped stone arch is visible at the left edge in the upper quarter and a second curved stone arch is clipped by the bottom left-middle. Continue these open waterways and paths, terrain, palette and scale while keeping the petal-pool flower unique.

tiles.title: The Reedvault Garden
tiles.description: Tall open limestone reed vaults shelter waterfalls and lily pools among golden stair paths and flowering garden islands.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (2,-1), directly east of The Petalwell Garden. Detailed dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water and restrained coral flowers at the established high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale, with soft upper-left light. A tall cluster of pale cream pointed limestone reed arches fills the center-right, with thin white waterfalls descending inside several open vaults into teal lily pools. Golden stair paths pass between the arched stems and wind among blocky planted limestone terraces, slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, small yellow and white flowers, coral flowering shrubs and trees, and pale faceted leaves. A small cream stone footbridge crosses a channel below the main vaults in the lower-right middle. The golden path enters the left edge near the upper quarter; teal channels continue the western neighbor at middle and lower heights with cropped cream limestone banks and plants. Golden paths remain open at the top near the left quarter and middle, at the right in the lower-middle, and at the bottom in the right-middle. Teal waterways remain open at the top near the left quarter and right-middle, along the right at upper, middle and lower heights, and across lower-left and lower-right portions of the bottom edge. A cropped stone arch is visible at the left upper edge and another at the bottom left-middle. Continue these open paths, water channels, planted ledges, medium and scale; keep the large reed-vault cluster unique.

tiles.title: The Shellspring Terraces
tiles.description: A curled limestone shell cradles a teal lily pool and spills small waterfalls into planted terraces threaded by golden stair paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (2,0), below The Reedvault Garden and east of The Rootglass Orchard. Detailed dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water, restrained coral flowers, same high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale with soft upper-left light. A broad pale cream limestone shell fills the center, its curled inner whorl and high ridged left wall enclosing a teal pool with green lily pads and pale coral-white blossoms. Thin white waterfalls spill from its lip to branching channels among planted blocky limestone ledges. Golden paths wind through short cream stairs; a small arched stone footbridge crosses the lower-right channel. Slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, small yellow and white flowers, coral flowering shrubs, pale faceted leaves and a few pointed rock outcrops fill the terraces. The top boundary carries teal water near the left sixth and far right, a cropped cream arch toward the left quarter, and a golden path just right of center. The left edge carries teal channels through its upper and middle portions and golden paths at middle and lower heights. Golden paths remain open at the right around middle and lower-middle heights. Teal water remains open along the right in upper, middle and lower portions, and at the bottom near the middle and far right. A cropped small cream arch sits at the lower-left portion of the bottom edge. Continue these waterways, planted limestone ledges, paths, medium and scale; keep the central shell spring unique.

tiles.title: The Reedharp Fen
tiles.description: A pale limestone harp suspends thin waterfall strings above a lily-filled fen threaded with golden paths and planted stone terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (2,1), south of The Shellspring Terraces and east of The Ammonite Mere. Detailed dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water, restrained coral flowers, high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and soft upper-left light. A tall pale limestone harp dominates the center, its curved upper beam joining uneven upright sides and suspending thin vertical waterfall strings into a teal lily basin. White cascades descend through blocky limestone ledges around it. Slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, little white and ochre flowers, coral flowering shrubs and several pale faceted leaf clusters fill the planted terraces. Golden paths wind through short cream stairs, with a small cream footbridge at lower right and cream arches in the upper-left and cropped lower-left corners. The top edge carries a teal channel near the middle and water at the far right, a cropped cream arch near the left, and golden path near the left and just right of center. The left boundary carries water through upper and middle portions and golden paths around middle and lower-middle heights. Water stays open at the right in upper, middle and bottom portions, with golden path exits around upper-middle and lower-middle heights. At the bottom, water exits right of center and at the far right, and golden paths exit near the left sixth and near the middle. Continue the connected wetland channels, cream limestone terraces, paths, medium and scale; keep the central waterfall harp unique.

tiles.title: The Stonepetal Reservoir
tiles.description: A giant limestone water lily cradles tiered teal pools that spill into a lush network of wetland channels and golden garden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (2,2), directly south of The Reedharp Fen. Detailed dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water, restrained coral flowers, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and soft upper-left light. A giant cream limestone water lily fills the center: tall veined rear petals rise behind a central lily pool, while lower cupped petals hold smaller teal pools and spill white cascades into surrounding channels. Blocky cream limestone banks and pillars divide planted islets with dark cypresses, long reeds, white irises, tiny white and ochre flowers, coral shrubs and a few pale faceted leaf clusters. Golden paths pass through cream stair flights; a cream arched footbridge crosses the channel at lower right, and a cropped cream arch appears at upper left. The top edge continues golden paths near the left fifth and near the middle, plus water right of center and at the far right. Channels remain open along upper portions of both side edges and through the right-middle area; golden paths reach both sides at several heights. At the bottom, golden paths reach the edge left of center and near the right, and teal water reaches the lower edge right of center. Continue the wetland channels, low limestone terraces, garden planting, medium and scale; keep the giant stone blossom unique.

tiles.title: The Hourglass Fen
tiles.description: A cream limestone hourglass fountain pours between two lily pools amid verdigris wetlands and winding golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (1,2), directly west of The Stonepetal Reservoir and south of The Ammonite Mere. Detailed dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water, restrained coral flowers, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and upper-left light. The central cream-limestone fountain has a broad circular upper lily pool, a tapered hourglass-shaped stone waist and a larger lower lily pool; a long white cascade falls from the upper front lip into the lower pool, and several short cascades spill from the lower rim into surrounding channels. Blocky limestone banks and pillars divide densely planted islets with dark cypresses, long reeds, white irises, yellow and white flowers, coral clusters and pale faceted leaves. Golden paths wind through cream stair flights, and a cream arched bridge crosses the lower-right channel. Paths reach the top left of center and near the middle, with teal water toward the top right. The right boundary carries the upper channel and several golden path sections, adjoining the reservoir's limestone wetland terrain. Golden paths remain open at several points along the left edge and near the bottom center-left; teal water reaches the bottom right of center. Continue these channels, garden paths, low limestone terraces, medium and scale; keep the stone hourglass fountain unique.

tiles.title: The Stonefern Rills
tiles.description: A great curled limestone fern sheds slender rills into lily-filled channels among flowered terraces and golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (0,2), south of The Droplet Willow and west of The Hourglass Fen. Dense dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water, restrained coral flowers, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and upper-left light. A great cream-limestone fern rises from a planted islet left of center, with five broad ribbed fronds curling into tight spirals; slender white rills fall from several curled tips into the channels below. Several short cascades descend between low blocky limestone terraces. Dark cypresses, long reeds, white irises, small yellow and white flowers, coral clusters and pale faceted leaves line the banks. Small green lily pads and pale flowers float in the teal channels. A cream arched footbridge crosses the channel in the lower-right-middle. Gold paths and short cream stairs reach the top near two-fifths width, the left edge around middle height, the right edge at upper-middle and lower-middle, and the bottom left of center. Teal water remains open at the top center-right and bottom near center and right of center. Continue wetland channels, low stone terraces, gold trails, palette and scale; keep the curled stone fern unique.

tiles.title: The Tideglass Gate
tiles.description: An upright limestone arch holds a shimmering teal pool above winding streams, gold paths and flowered wetland terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-1,2), south of The Levity Wells and west of The Stonefern Rills. Dense dark ink contours and fine crosshatching, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal channels, restrained coral flowers, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and upper-left light. Slightly left of center stands a tall oval cream-limestone arch on a low planted islet; its opening holds a glossy teal water surface with reflected vegetation, and several thin white rills spill from its lower rim. Short cascades run between low blocky limestone terraces around it. Slim dark cypresses, long reeds, white irises, tiny yellow and white flowers, coral clusters and pale faceted leaves line the channels, with green lily pads and pale water lilies. One small cream arched footbridge crosses the channel right of center in the lower-middle. Gold paths and cream stairs reach the top in the right half, the left edge in the upper quarter and around middle height, the right edge in the upper-middle and lower-middle, and the bottom right of center. Open teal water reaches the top across the left-middle and at the upper-right corner, the left lower edge, and the bottom near the left quarter and across the center-right. Continue the northern and eastern neighbors' rocky wetland channels, low terraces, gold trails, palette and scale; keep the vertical water arch unique.

tiles.title: The Shellspring Fen
tiles.description: A ribbed limestone shell cradles a lily-covered spring among stepped wetland channels and winding golden garden trails.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-2,2), west of The Tideglass Gate. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippled foliage, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, midnight-teal water, cream limestone, restrained coral flowers, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and upper-left light. Just left of center is a large open cream-limestone shell spring with a tall scalloped ribbed back, curved pale inner steps, and a round teal basin containing green lily pads and one pale water lily; three thin white cascades spill from its lower rim. Low blocky limestone terraces divide branching marsh channels, with more short cascades. Slim dark cypresses, dense reeds, white irises, tiny yellow and white flowers, coral clusters and large pale faceted leaves fill the islets. Golden paths with cream stair flights cross the top and both sides and continue toward the bottom left of center. On the shared eastern/right edge, gold paths exit in the upper-middle and lower-middle, with teal wetland water toward the upper-right and lower-right corners; continue the neighboring tile's limestone planting, trail scale and channels. Open teal water also reaches the top left of center, the upper-left edge, and across much of the bottom center and right. Keep the ribbed shell spring unique when adding the next region.

tiles.title: The Fernvault Crossing
tiles.description: A giant pale fern carries a golden stair-path above branching marsh channels and flowering limestone terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-2,1), north of The Shellspring Fen and west of The Levity Wells. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippled foliage, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; midnight-teal water, cream limestone, restrained coral flowers, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and upper-left light. A giant pale cream fern rises from a small walled limestone islet left of center, its curling frond arching above the water with a coiled tip near the upper-left center; a slender golden trail follows the frond's spine and descends by cream stairs on its right into the bank paths. Smaller ferns cluster at its base. Branching lily-pad channels, pale water lilies, short white cascades, blocky limestone terraces, slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, small yellow and white flowers, coral clusters and pale faceted leaves fill the terrain. At the shared southern/bottom edge, teal channels remain open on both sides of the golden path and stairs reaching the bottom near the center. On the shared eastern/right edge, golden paths and stair flights reach the upper-middle and middle/lower portions, with teal channels between planted limestone ledges. Open teal water and trails also reach the top and left edges. Continue the wetland channels and slender gold paths at this scale; keep the enormous fern crossing unique.

tiles.title: The Rainseed Hollow

tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-2,0), directly north of The Fernvault Crossing and west of The Tide Harp. tiles.title: The Woven Cascade
tiles.description: A looping limestone aqueduct pours a white cascade into a lily-filled wetland garden threaded by golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-2,-1), directly north of The Rainseed Hollow and west of The Rainseed Orchard. A large pale cream limestone ribbon forms one open circular loop left of center, with a narrow teal aqueduct along its upper curve and a white waterfall descending from the right tip into a rippled midnight-teal pond. tiles.title: The Stonefern Wells

At the northern/top boundary a golden path exits near the left fifth and teal water remains open across the upper middle. Slim dark cypresses, white irises, ochre-white stippled flower carpets, restrained coral blossoms and pale faceted leaves surround the landmark. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; upper-left light, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the water, golden trails, stair flights and planted limestone terrain; keep the stone fern landmark unique.

tiles.title: The Conchwater Chambers
tiles.description: A great limestone conch cradles cascading teal pools above a flowering wetland crossed by golden stair paths and a small stone bridge.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-1,-2), directly east of The Stonefern Wells and north of The Rainseed Orchard. One large ivory limestone conch rises in the upper middle, its pointed spiral whorls extending toward the upper right and its broad open lip facing lower left; two exposed teal basin chambers spill in thin white waterfalls into the surrounding waterways. The conch is covered in small verdigris vines and ochre-white blossoms, and remains distinct from the stone fern and water-bowl tree. Midnight-teal river channels wind from the upper middle around the conch through cream block terraces and down to the bottom around the left quarter to left middle; lily pads and pale peach-white lilies float among reeds. A low arched cream stone bridge crosses the right-hand channel below center, with golden paths and cream stair flights on both approaches. Golden trails meet the left edge around the upper third and lower quarter, amid open teal side channels and planted limestone terrain, continuing the west neighbor. At the bottom boundary, open teal water reaches the edge around the left quarter and a golden stair path exits just right of center, continuing the southern orchard's top-edge water and path. Teal water remains open at the top across the middle and in patches on the right edge; golden paths exit the top near the left quarter and the right edge around the upper third and lower quarter. Slim dark cypresses, white irises, pale faceted leaves, stippled ochre-white flower carpets and restrained coral blossoms surround the pools and paths. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling with verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; upper-left lighting, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the rivers, trails, stair flights and planted limestone terraces while keeping the conch landmark unique.

tiles.title: The Rainstring Lyre
tiles.description: A vine-covered limestone lyre pours waterfall strings into teal pools among golden stair paths and flowering terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (0,-2), directly east of The Conchwater Chambers and north of The Suspended Ford. One large ivory limestone lyre stands in the upper middle-right, with two curled upright arms, a straight lintel and several slender white waterfall strings falling into a teal pool within its open U-shaped base. Verdigris vines and small ochre-white blossoms cover the lyre frame; the basin spills down a front limestone lip into the surrounding waterways. Midnight-teal river channels wind through cream block terraces, with lily pads, pale peach-white lilies, many short white cascades and ripples. A low arched cream stone bridge crosses a right-middle channel below center, with golden trails and cream stair flights on both approaches. Golden trails meet the left edge around the upper third and lower quarter, amid open teal side channels and planted limestone terrain, continuing the west neighbor. At the bottom boundary, teal water reaches the edge across the left-middle and a golden stair path exits just right of center, continuing the southern ford's top-edge water and path. Water remains open at the top across the middle and in patches on the right edge; golden paths exit the top near the left quarter and the right edge around the upper third and lower half. Slim dark cypresses, white irises, reeds, pale faceted leaves, stippled ochre-white flower carpets and restrained coral blossoms surround the channels and paths. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling with verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; upper-left lighting and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the waterways, golden trails, stair flights and planted limestone terraces while keeping this waterfall-string lyre unique.

tiles.title: The Fiddlehead Cascade
tiles.description: A curled limestone fern releases slender waterfalls into lily-filled teal channels amid golden stair trails and planted terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (1,-2), east of The Rainstring Lyre and north of The Petalwell Garden. One large ivory limestone fiddlehead fountain stands in the upper middle: its tightly curled spiral top rises above several long curved stone ribs holding shallow teal channels, with slender white cascades falling from their left-hand ends into the pool below. Verdigris vines and tiny ochre-white flowers climb the stone. Midnight-teal waterways wind between cream block terraces, with pale green lily pads, pale peach-white water lilies, small white cascades and fine white ripple lines. A low cream arched footbridge crosses a channel in the lower-right middle, with golden paths and short stair flights on both approaches. Golden stair trails reach the left edge around the upper third and lower quarter; teal water opens on the left around the middle amid planted limestone banks. Along the bottom edge, teal water remains open in the left-middle and just right of center, while a golden stair trail exits near the center. At the top, teal water is open in the left-middle and near the right corner, and a golden stair trail enters right of center. Teal channels continue through the right edge near the middle and lower portions, with a golden path crossing that edge below the middle. Tall slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, pale faceted leaves, dense ochre-white flower carpets and restrained coral flowers fill the planted terraces. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling with verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; upper-left light and the same high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the channels, golden stair trails, cream limestone banks and planted terrain while keeping this curled fern fountain unique.

tiles.title: The Seedcup Cascade
tiles.description: An opened ivory limestone seedcup spills slender waterfalls into winding lily canals above a golden path and cream arched footbridge.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (2,-2), east of The Fiddlehead Cascade and north of The Reedvault Garden. One large opened ivory limestone seedcup fountain occupies the upper middle, with rounded upright cup segments enclosing a shallow teal lily reservoir, a short stone stem, trailing ochre-green vines and slender white falls spilling into the surrounding canal. A low cream arched footbridge with round-topped posts crosses the canal right of center. Golden paths and stair flights wind between cream block limestone terraces, slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, pale faceted leaves, small white and ochre flowers, and restrained coral flowers. Midnight-teal waterways contain green lily pads, peach-white lilies, small bank cascades and fine pale ripple marks. Along the left edge, teal water remains open around the middle and lower portions, and golden paths enter near the upper-middle and lower quarter. At the bottom, a golden stair trail exits left of center, a small golden trail reaches the far right corner, and teal waterways remain open near the left corner and just right of center. At the top, a golden stair trail enters near the left corner, another golden path touches the middle area, and teal water remains open across the right portion. Along the right edge, teal channels remain open in the upper-middle and middle-lower portions, with a golden path reaching the edge below the middle. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; soft upper-left light and the established high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the canals, golden stairs, planted limestone banks and open exits while keeping the seedcup fountain unique.

tiles.title: The Hollowleaf Arcade
tiles.description: An airy limestone leaf arcade arches over golden stairs and a lily canal among flowering terraces and slender cypresses.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (3,-2), east of The Seedcup Cascade. One large pierced ivory limestone leaf arcade occupies the upper-middle and right: a diagonal spine rises to a pointed upper-right tip, with curved branching ribs forming open vaults over a teal lily canal and an ochre stair trail; ochre-green vines drape from the ribs. Golden paths and cream stair flights wind between block limestone banks, slender dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, pale faceted green leaves, white and ochre flowers and restrained coral blooms. Teal channels contain green lily pads, peach-white lilies, pale ripples and small white bank cascades. Teal water reaches the left edge at the upper corner and around the upper-middle and middle-lower portions; an ochre path enters the left edge near the lower quarter and connects to descending stairs. At the top, golden stair/path exits appear left of center and near the middle, while teal water stays open across much of the right portion. At the right edge, teal water remains open in the upper and middle portions, with a golden path reaching the edge in the lower-middle and near the bottom corner. At the bottom, teal channels remain open left of center and across the lower-right area beside the final golden stair trail near the right corner. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; soft upper-left light and high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue canals, planted limestone banks and golden stair paths, keeping the leaf arcade unique.

tiles.title: The Conchfall Garden
tiles.description: A vine-draped ivory conch fountain pours through scalloped basins into lily canals among golden stair paths and planted limestone terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (3,-1), south of The Hollowleaf Arcade and east of The Reedvault Garden. A large ivory limestone conch fountain occupies the center-right, with a curled spiral at its right side, tall curved ribbed shell surfaces draped in ochre-green vines, and a descending sequence of open scalloped basins along its left side; thin white cascades connect the basins and fall into the teal canal below. Golden paths and cream stair flights wind diagonally between block limestone planted banks, slender dark cypresses, reeds, white irises, pale faceted leaves, white and ochre flowers, and restrained coral shrubs. Teal canals contain green lily pads, peach-white lilies, pale ripples and small bank waterfalls. At the top edge teal water remains open near the left corner and across portions of the right half, with a golden stair/path exit left of center. Along the left edge, teal channels remain open at upper, middle and lower heights and an ochre path enters around the lower-middle before descending cream stairs. At the right edge, water remains open in upper and middle portions, with ochre path openings around the lower-middle and near the bottom corner. At the bottom, teal water remains open across much of the left and center-right portions beside planted banks; a golden path reaches the lower-right corner. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; soft upper-left light and high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the open canals, planted limestone banks and golden stair paths while keeping the conch fountain unique.

tiles.title: The Dewbell Grove
tiles.description: An ivory root-tree carries hanging bell fountains that pour into a lily pool amid stepped limestone gardens and golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (3,0), south of The Conchfall Garden and east of The Shellspring Terraces. A large ivory limestone tree occupies the center-right, with twisting roots, arched openings sheltering golden paths, curved branches draped in ochre-green vines, and multiple pale bell-shaped flowers hanging from its branches. Thin white streams fall from the bells into a rounded teal pool with green lily pads and peach-white lilies; small waterfalls spill from its planted limestone rim into branching lower canals. Golden paths and short cream stair flights wind between block limestone planted banks, slender dark cypresses, reeds, white irises and daisies, pale faceted leaves, ochre flowers, and restrained coral flowering shrubs. Top edge opens onto teal water across the left portion and center-right, separated by planted banks, with a golden stair-path reaching the upper-right corner. Left edge carries open teal water at upper, middle and lower heights and a golden stair-path entrance around the middle. Right edge leaves water open around the middle and golden paths open in upper and lower portions. Bottom edge leaves teal water open across the left and center-right portions, a golden path near the center-left, and a golden path near the lower-right corner. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; soft upper-left light and high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue canals, planted limestone banks and golden stairs; keep the root-tree with hanging bell fountains unique.

tiles.title: The Petalspill Cistern
tiles.description: An ivory limestone lotus holds teal water in its carved petals and spills slender waterfalls into a lily basin among planted terraces and golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (3,1), south of The Dewbell Grove and east of The Reedharp Fen. A large ivory limestone lotus fountain fills the center-right: several open carved petals hold shallow teal pools around a taller pointed central bud, with small ochre-green vines draping the stone and thin white waterfalls descending from the petal rims into the surrounding lily basin. Green lily pads and cream-coral lotus flowers float in branching midnight-teal canals; small white cascades spill over planted block-limestone banks. Golden paths wind between short cream stairs, a low cream arched footbridge in the lower-left quadrant, slim dark cypresses, reeds, white irises and daisies, ochre flowers, pale faceted leaf clusters and restrained coral shrubs. The top edge carries teal water across the left and center-right portions and golden paths around center-left and near the right corner. The left edge has open water in upper, middle and lower portions and a broad golden path entrance around upper-middle height. The right edge opens to water around the middle and lower portions, with golden paths toward the upper and lower corners. The bottom edge carries water across the left portion and center-right, a golden path near the center, and a golden stair-path near the right corner. Detailed deep ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, soft upper-left light and high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the canals, planted limestone terraces and golden paths; keep the petal-pool lotus fountain unique.

tiles.title: The Shellspill Arcade
tiles.description: An open limestone spiral holds lily-filled pools that spill into branching canals amid golden paths and planted terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (3,2), south of The Petalspill Cistern and east of The Stonepetal Reservoir. A large ivory limestone spiral water arcade fills the center-right: curved open walls coil around a small inner pool, with green lily pads in successive shallow teal chambers, ochre-green vines draping the stone, and thin white waterfalls descending from several rims into the surrounding canals. Cream-coral lotus flowers and lily pads float in branching midnight-teal water. A low cream arched footbridge crosses a channel in the lower-left quadrant. Golden paths pass through short cream stair flights between planted block-limestone banks, dark narrow cypresses, long reeds, white irises and daisies, ochre flowers, coral flower clusters, and pale faceted leaves. The top edge opens to water across the left portion and center-right, with golden path and stair entrances near the center and right corner. The left edge carries open water in upper and middle-to-lower portions and golden paths around middle and lower-middle heights, continuing the west neighbor's channels and terraces. The right edge has golden paths and stairs in upper and middle portions and teal water near the lower corner. The bottom edge opens to teal water in the left portion and right quarter, with a golden path near the center. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the canals, limestone planting terraces and golden paths; keep the coiled stone water arcade unique.

tiles.title: The Reedspill Grove
tiles.description: Hollow limestone reeds pour slender waterfalls into small tiered basins amid teal canals, golden stair paths and flowering garden banks.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (3,3), directly south of The Shellspill Arcade. A fan-like grove of tall cream limestone hollow reeds occupies center-left; their rounded cupped openings pour thin white waterfalls, with ochre-green vines trailing down their stems. Several small semicircular stone basins step through the lower part of the grove and spill into surrounding midnight-teal canals. A low cream arched footbridge crosses the lower-right channel. Golden paths enter from the top near center, descend short ivory stair flights, wind down the right side, and continue toward the bottom center-right; a stair path also reaches the right edge around mid-height. The top edge has teal water at the left portion and across the right quarter, continuing the northern neighbor's bottom-edge waterways, and a central golden stair-path entrance. Open teal water touches the left edge at several upper and middle-to-lower stretches and the right edge in upper and lower portions. At the bottom, teal channels remain open at the left portion and near the right corner, with the golden path between them. Planted cream block-limestone banks carry narrow dark cypresses, long verdigris reeds, white irises and daisies, ochre flowers, restrained coral flower clusters, and pale broad faceted leaves; green lily pads and cream-coral lotus blossoms float in the canals. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the branching canals, limestone banks and golden stair paths, keeping the hollow stone-reed fountain grove unique.

tiles.title: The Ribbonwater Court
tiles.description: A curved limestone aqueduct pours slender waterfalls into stepped garden pools among teal canals and golden stair paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (2,3), directly south of The Stonepetal Reservoir and west of The Reedspill Grove. A broad cream limestone aqueduct rises in a curved arch across center-left and bends down toward center-right, its shallow teal trough spilling thin white cascades into a sequence of small round lower basins. A larger round pool sits at center-right behind the aqueduct; the pools contain green lily pads, with a cream-coral lotus in the larger basin. Ochre-green vines hang over the aqueduct masonry and low block-limestone banks. One low cream arched footbridge crosses the lower-right channel. Golden paths enter the top left of center and near the right, descend short ivory stair flights and wind along both sides of the central waterwork; a path reaches the left edge around the middle-to-lower portion, and the right path continues to the bottom-right corner. Open midnight-teal water reaches the top at the left and in upper-center/right stretches, the left edge through upper and lower portions, the right edge in several upper and middle-to-lower stretches, and the bottom at the left and center-right. Planted banks carry narrow dark cypresses, long verdigris reeds, white irises and daisies, tiny ochre flowers, restrained coral clusters, and pale broad faceted leaves; green lily pads and sparse cream-coral lotus blossoms float in the canals. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue branching canals, cream limestone terraces and golden stair paths across the open exits, keeping this curved aqueduct and stepped round basins unique.

tiles.title: The Stoneleaf Confluence
tiles.description: A raised leaf-shaped limestone water garden divides lily-filled teal pools with branching stone veins and spills white cascades into the surrounding canals.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (1,3), directly south of The Hourglass Fen and west of The Ribbonwater Court. The central landmark is a broad leaf-shaped cream limestone water garden raised on short block-masonry pillars, with a central cream stem and branching stone ribs separating elongated midnight-teal lily pools; green lily pads and cream-coral lotus blossoms sit inside, and narrow white cascades fall from the outer rim into surrounding canals. Ochre-green vines drape the leaf rim, pillars and low limestone banks. A low cream arched footbridge crosses the lower center-left channel. Golden paths enter at the top left of center, descend two short stair flights behind the leaf, reach the left boundary around the middle-to-lower portion, cross the lower footbridge, and continue through ivory steps to the bottom right of center; a separate golden path and ivory stair flight reach the right edge around the middle. Teal channels stay open along the top left and upper center-right, the right upper and lower portions, the left upper and lower portions, and the bottom at the left, center-left and right. Banks are densely planted with narrow dark cypresses, long verdigris reeds, white irises and daisies, small ochre blossoms, restrained coral clusters and pale broad faceted leaves; lily pads and sparse lotus flowers float in the surrounding water. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the canals, cream limestone banks and golden stair paths across open exits, keeping the raised stone leaf unique.

tiles.title: The Rainharp Hollow
tiles.description: A vine-draped limestone rain harp suspends fine water ribbons above a scalloped pool among flowered canals and golden stair paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (0,3), directly south of The Stonefern Rills and west of The Stoneleaf Confluence. A tall rounded cream block-limestone arch stands at the center over a low scalloped teal pool, with several thin vertical white water ribbons descending from its underside to concentric ripples in the basin; ochre-green vines drape the arch, pool rim and masonry banks. A low cream arched footbridge crosses a canal in the lower-left-middle. A golden path enters the top left of center, descends cream stair flights and runs behind the central arch. Another golden path enters the left around middle height, reaches the lower footbridge, crosses to the lower center and descends ivory steps toward the bottom right of center. Golden stairs and a path reach the right edge around middle height. Midnight-teal water remains open at the top center-right and far right, along the left upper and lower portions, along the right upper and lower portions, and at the bottom left, center-left and far right. Short white cascades fall between cream masonry terraces into surrounding canals. Dense narrow dark cypresses, long verdigris reeds, white irises and daisies, tiny ochre blossoms, coral flower clusters and pale broad veined leaves line the banks; green lily pads and sparse cream-coral lotus flowers float in the water. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue canals, golden stair paths and low limestone banks across open exits; keep the rain-harp arch unique.

tiles.title: The Shellstep Spring
tiles.description: A low limestone spiral spring curls through a planted wetland of teal canals, golden stair paths and small cascading rills.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-1,3), directly south of The Tideglass Gate and west of The Rainharp Hollow. A broad low cream block-limestone spiral spring fills the center-left, with a teal channel winding around a tightly curled inner masonry wall; ochre-green vines drape its banks, thin white rills descend from the rear rim into the spiral, and a wider white cascade falls over the front lip into the surrounding channel. A low cream arched footbridge with round finials crosses a canal at lower-right-middle. Golden paths and ivory stairs reach the top just right of center, the left edge in the upper quarter and near middle height, the right edge in the lower-middle, and the bottom right of center. Open teal water reaches the top across left-middle and at far right, the right edge above and below the bridge path, and the bottom near the left quarter and at far right. Low cream masonry terraces and short white cascades line the canals. Dense narrow dark cypresses, long verdigris reeds, white irises and daisies, tiny ochre blossoms, coral flower clusters and pale broad veined leaves grow along the banks; green lily pads and cream-coral lotus flowers float in the water. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue open canals, golden stair paths and low planted limestone banks across the western and southern exits; keep the central shell spiral unique.

tiles.title: The Willowglass Reach
tiles.description: A bowed willow pours delicate streams from pale hanging leaves into branching canals among planted limestone weirs and golden stair paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-2,3), directly south of The Shellspring Fen and west of The Shellstep Spring. A large bowed willow grows from a low planted cream-limestone island near the center, with a twisting ochre-brown trunk and airy hanging sprays of pale veined verdigris leaves across the center-left; thin white streams fall from several leaf tips into the surrounding teal canal, forming small circular ripples. Low block-limestone weirs carry short white cascades throughout branching waterways, with golden ochre paths and ivory stair flights between planted banks. Golden paths reach the top left of center, the right edge in the upper eighth and near middle height, the left edge in the upper quarter and around middle and lower-middle heights, and the bottom right of center. Open teal water reaches the top around the left quarter and across the right half, the right edge between the trail exits and below them, and the bottom across the left quarter and far right. Dense narrow dark cypresses, long verdigris reeds, white irises and small white flowers, ochre blossoms, restrained coral clusters and pale broad veined leaves line the banks; green lily pads and cream-coral lotus flowers float in the channels. Detailed dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the open western and southern canals and stair paths while keeping the stream-bearing willow unique.

tiles.title: The Stonefern Crossing
tiles.description: A curled limestone fern sends golden footpaths over branching teal canals between flowered banks and small cascading weirs.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-3,3), immediately west of The Willowglass Reach. A large pale cream limestone fern rises from a planted central island, with a tightly curled fiddlehead left of upper center and finely divided stone fronds that arch over the canals. Ochre walking surfaces run along three broad fern ribs toward the middle-left, lower-middle right and bottom right-of-center; ivory stair flights join them to bank paths. Branching midnight-teal canals contain green lily pads and cream-coral lotus flowers. Low cream block-limestone weirs carry short white cascades with radial ripples. Dense dark narrow cypresses, verdigris reeds, white irises and small white flowers, ochre blossoms, restrained coral flowers and broad pale veined leaves line the banks. Golden paths reach the top left of center, the left edge in the upper fifth and near the middle, the right edge around the upper quarter and lower-middle, and the bottom right of center. Teal water remains open at top around the left quarter and right half, along the left between path banks and across the lower portion, on the right between path exits and across the lower quarter, and at the bottom across the left half and far right. Right-edge canals and ochre stair paths continue the eastern neighbor's garden terrain. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment; upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature scale. Continue open canals and paths on the western, northern and southern edges while keeping the stone fern crossing unique.

tiles.title: The Rainseed Court
tiles.description: A ribbed limestone seedpod releases three slender waterfalls into a lily-filled pool among golden paths and planted marsh terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-3,2), north of The Stonefern Crossing and west of The Shellspring Fen. A large upright cream-limestone seedpod fountain stands above the central pool, with a pointed crown, fine vertical ribs and three dark rounded openings that release long thin white waterfalls. Two curved outer stone supports and one straight central stem descend toward the water; low broken cream stone banks encircle parts of the lily-filled pool. Branching midnight-teal channels contain olive-green lily pads and cream lotus flowers edged with restrained coral. Block-limestone weirs carry short white cascades and radial ripples. Dense narrow dark cypresses, verdigris reeds, white irises, tiny ochre blossoms, coral flowers and broad pale veined leaves fill the islets. Ochre paths and cream stairs reach the top left of center, the left edge in the upper fifth and near the middle, the right edge across the middle and lower-middle, and the bottom around the left-of-center two-fifths. Open teal water reaches the top around the left sixth and right half, the left between planted path banks and across the lower portion, the right near the upper quarter and lower fifth, and the bottom across much of the left third and far right. The bottom ochre path and teal waterways continue toward the southern fern region; right-edge planted banks, paths and canals continue toward the eastern shell fen. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, warm cream stone, verdigris and ochre watercolor on parchment; coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature scale and upper-left light. Continue open canals and walking paths toward the northern and western edges, keeping the elevated seedpod fountain unique.

tiles.title: The Ivory Fan
tiles.description: A broad ribbed limestone fan spans lily canals, joining cream steps and golden trails among flowered garden banks.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-3,1), north of The Rainseed Court and west of The Fernvault Crossing. A huge cream-limestone fan dominates the center: a scalloped upper rim, deeply incised radiating ribs, dense fine hatching and stippling, a narrow curved tapering stem at the lower-left front, and curved descending step-like ribs toward the lower-right. Trailing small ochre foliage crosses its face and hangs from the rim; cream stairs connect the stem to an ochre path below. Midnight-teal channels wind beneath and around the fan, filled with olive lily pads and cream lotus flowers edged with restrained coral. Short white cascades spill from block-limestone weirs into radial white ripples. Dense dark cypresses, narrow verdigris reeds, white irises, small ochre flowers, coral flower clusters and broad pale veined leaves fill the stone-banked islets. At the bottom, the golden path exits right of center near three-fifths, while teal canals remain open across much of the left third and far right; these continue toward the southern Rainseed region. At the right, a golden path and cream stairs reach the middle to lower-middle edge between planted banks, while teal channels stay open above and below toward the eastern fern region. An ochre trail exits the top left of center and the left near the upper fifth; teal channels also reach the top across the middle-right and far right and the left across the lower portion. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor, warm cream limestone and parchment highlights; coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale with upper-left light. Continue the open canals and golden trails toward the north and west, keeping the giant ribbed fan unique.

tiles.title: The Braided Spring
tiles.description: Interlaced limestone ribbons arch over lily-filled canals amid golden stair paths and densely planted wetland terraces.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-3,0), directly north of The Ivory Fan and west of The Rainseed Hollow. Broad cream-limestone ribbons interlace into a low arched root-knot in the central-left garden, with fine longitudinal grooves, ink hatching and trailing ochre plants. Thin white streams descend beneath the arches into midnight-teal water with circular white ripples. Surrounding canals contain olive lily pads and cream lotus flowers edged with restrained coral; short white cascades fall from block-limestone weirs. Golden paths and cream stairs wind around stone-banked islets planted with slim dark cypresses, tall verdigris reeds, white irises, small ochre flowers, coral flower clusters and broad pale veined leaves. At the bottom, an ochre path exits left of center near the first third, while broad teal channels remain open across the middle-right and far right toward the southern Ivory Fan region. At the right, ochre stair paths reach the upper-middle and lower-middle edge between planted limestone banks, with teal water open above, between and below toward the eastern Rainseed region. An ochre trail exits the top left of center, and golden paths also reach the left in its upper-middle and lower portions; teal water remains open at the top and left around planted banks. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor, warm cream limestone and parchment highlights; coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale with upper-left light. Continue the open canals and golden trails toward the north and west while keeping the interlaced stone spring unique.

tiles.title: The Stone Blossom Well
tiles.description: Folded limestone petals cradle a lily pool and spill white streams into the surrounding garden canals.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-3,-1), directly north of The Braided Spring and west of The Woven Cascade. Broad pale cream limestone petals fold outward around a central midnight-teal pool containing olive lily pads and cream lotus flowers edged with coral; narrow white streams fall from the petal tips and clefts into surrounding canals with fine circular ripples. Ochre flowering vines trail across the stone petals. Branching teal water channels pass between low block-limestone banks, golden paths and short cream stairs. Garden islets contain slim dark cypresses, tall verdigris reeds, white irises, tiny ochre-white flowers, restrained coral blossom clusters and broad pale veined leaves. At the bottom an ochre stair path exits near the first third, with teal water open centrally and along the right toward the southern Braided Spring. At the right an ochre stair path meets the edge around mid-height; teal channels remain open above and below toward the eastern Woven Cascade. A golden path exits the top left of center, while teal water reaches the top on both sides of planted banks. Golden paths reach the left in its upper-middle and lower portions, with teal water open between them. Detailed dark ink contours, fine longitudinal hatching and stippling, translucent verdigris and ochre watercolor on warm parchment, pale limestone highlights, high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale and upper-left light. tiles.title: The Folded Rill

At the bottom an ochre stair trail reaches the edge just left of center, with open teal water along the left, near the center-right and at the far right toward the southern blossom well. At the right an ochre stair path reaches the edge near mid-height, with teal wetland water open above it and in the lower portion toward the eastern stonefern region. tiles.title: The Rainleaf Grove
tiles.description: A branching limestone tree holds three water-filled stone leaves that spill slender streams into a flower-lined teal canal garden.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-3,-3), directly north of The Folded Rill. White flowers and trailing golden vines cover parts of the leaves and trunk. Low cream block banks and short pillars surround the island and planted margins, with dark slender cypresses, tall verdigris reeds, white irises, ochre-white flowers, coral star flowers and pale veined foliage. The ochre path exits the bottom slightly left of center, connecting toward the southern folded crossing; water remains open at the bottom left, center-right and far right. An ochre stair path exits the top left of center, with teal water open around it and toward both corners. At the left edge an ochre path enters near mid-height and crosses a small cream arched footbridge lower down. At the right edge ochre stair paths are open in the upper-middle and lower-middle portions, with teal water beside the planted banks. A short white spillway drops from the central island near its bottom and another appears near the bottom-right edge. tiles.title: The Ammonite Spring

A golden ochre trail with cream stair flights enters the western edge in the upper quarter, bends down the left side and exits the bottom near the left third. tiles.title: The Ivory Reef Rills

tiles.title: The Twinloop Rills

tiles.title: The Shellcurl Rills

Cream rectangular supports hold the shell above the canal; golden flowering vines and small white flowers drape over the roof, and narrow white falls spill from its rim and nearby block banks. tiles.title: The Leaflift Cascades

In the middle-right, a tall pale limestone stem branches into three open leaf-shaped basins: one high near the upper-middle, one to the right, and one lower on the left. Thin white falls descend from the bowls into the canals, with fine radiating ripples below. Gold-green flowering vines hang from bowl rims and pale block banks. tiles.title: The Pearlthread Weir

An open C-shaped ivory limestone aqueduct occupies center-right, opening toward the left; its raised crescent channel carries teal water between cream walls engraved with ochre leaves, and several white streams fall from its rim into pale concentric canal ripples. Gold-green vines with white daisies hang from the rim and its two rounded ends. A golden-orange stair trail enters the top around x=0.55, bends downward left of the crescent and meets an arched ivory stair footbridge around (0.35,0.59); a winding golden trail continues below the bridge, branching to the bottom around x=0.61 and to the right around y=0.65. Broad midnight-teal and verdigris canals with olive lily pads and cream coral-edged lotus blossoms continue through portions of all edges. Low ivory block banks, square cream posts with round finials, narrow dark cypresses, large ochre-veined teal leaves, white daisies and irises, restrained coral stars and reed tips, golden hanging growth, and small white bank waterfalls fill the garden.
