tiles.description: A curled limestone fern bridge carries a golden walkway and a spilling teal rill above a lily-filled canal garden.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-5,6), immediately south of The Seedwell Spillgarden and west of The Seedwell Cistern. A large cream limestone bridge runs diagonally from lower left toward upper right over the central midnight-teal canal, with curled scroll ends, carved upright leaf-shaped balustrades, an ochre golden walkway, and tapered arched piers. A narrow teal rill follows the near side of the bridge and spills blue-white cascades into concentric pale ripples beneath it; gold-green vines drape its rail and piers. Olive lily pads and three prominent cream-coral lotus blooms float in the surrounding canal. Low cream block banks with sphere-topped posts and small waterfall spillways border narrow midnight-teal cypresses, broad verdigris foliage with coral outlines, white daisies, coral star flowers, and ochre grasses. A golden route with cream stair flights enters the top near x=0.50, leads behind the bridge, descends from the bridge at lower left, and continues to the bottom near x=0.46. Golden stair-route exits reach the left and right around y=0.44, matching the eastern neighbor's western exit. Canal water remains open on both sides of the top and bottom routes and above and below the side routes. Strong dark ink contours, fine crosshatching, dense stippling, midnight teal, verdigris, ochre and restrained coral watercolor appearance on warm parchment-colored limestone; soft upper-left light and consistent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue western and southern water and route exits while keeping this leaf-balustraded curled bridge unique.

tiles.title: The Whisperreed Basin
tiles.description: A ringed limestone pool holds hollow reed fountains whose blue-white streams fall among lily pads beside golden stairways.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,6), immediately west of The Fernspan Rill. A near-circular midnight-teal pool slightly left of center is enclosed by a low cream limestone ring with sphere-topped posts and gold-green trailing vines. A tall cluster of cream hollow reed-shaped stone fountains rises from the pool, with ochre interiors, hooked and curled tips, several descending blue-white streams and one high arcing stream toward a curled mouth. Concentric pale ripples lie beneath the falls; olive lily pads and cream-coral lotus blooms occupy the pool and surrounding open water. Golden routes with short cream stair flights connect the ring to the left and right edges around y=0.44 and descend toward the bottom near x=0.48. The right route continues the eastern neighbor's western exit, with open teal canal above and below it. Teal water reaches the top and flows between planted banks at the left, right and bottom boundaries. Islands and low cream block walls carry narrow midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris leaves outlined in restrained coral, white daisies, coral star flowers, ochre grasses and tall cattails. Strong dark ink contours, fine crosshatching, dense stippling, midnight teal, verdigris, ochre and restrained coral watercolor appearance on warm parchment-colored limestone; soft upper-left illumination and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the western and southern water and golden route exits while keeping this hollow reed fountain cluster unique.

tiles.title: The Foldleaf Sluice
tiles.description: A curled limestone leaf carries a raised teal stream above a planted canal and pours five bright waterfalls into lily-filled water.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,5), immediately above The Whisperreed Basin and west of The Seedwell Spillgarden. An elongated pale cream limestone leaf trough runs diagonally from a pointed lower-left end to a curled upper-right tip on slim stone piers and arches. Carved leaf veins line its raised sides around a narrow midnight-teal central watercourse. Five blue-white falls pour from four rounded side openings and the curled upper tip into concentric pale ripple rings below. Golden ochre routes with short cream stair flights reach the top near x=0.49 and the left around y=0.46, threading between planted banks and behind the leaf; no path reaches the bottom or right edge. Open teal canal, olive lily pads and several cream-coral lotus blooms surround the structure. Low cream block walls and sphere-topped posts carry gold-green trailing vines; planted islands hold narrow midnight-teal cypresses, large verdigris leaves with coral veins, white daisies, coral star flowers, ochre grasses and cattails. The bottom edge continues the southern neighbor's northern water with planted corner banks; the right edge continues the eastern neighbor's western water and planted limestone banks without a road connection. Water also reaches the top and left between planted banks. Strong dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and dense stippling, midnight teal, verdigris, ochre and restrained coral watercolor appearance on warm parchment-colored limestone, soft upper-left illumination and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the northern and western golden routes and the open canals while keeping this folded limestone leaf sluice unique.

tiles.title: The Dewbell Court
tiles.description: A scalloped limestone bell shelters a suspended blue droplet above a round teal basin where four falls ripple through the planted canals.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,4), directly north of The Foldleaf Sluice and west of The Fanroot Crossing. A tall cream-limestone bell pavilion stands centrally above a circular midnight-teal basin, with a sphere finial, carved leaf-vein ribs, a broad scalloped roof and slim arched supports. One luminous blue droplet hangs above the basin's concentric ripple rings, with tiny droplets visible above and below it. Four blue-white falls descend from the two outer sides and two front basin openings into pale circular ripples in the surrounding canal. A golden ochre path and cream stair flights reach the bottom near x=0.53 and pass beneath the pavilion's front arch, continuing the southern neighbor's northern route. A winding golden path reaches the left edge around y=0.43. No golden path reaches the top or right edge. The right edge continues the eastern neighbor's western open-water intervals and planted limestone banks without a road join. Open teal water and planted banks reach the top; water continues on both sides of the bottom approach and around the left path. Low cream block walls and sphere-topped posts carry gold-green trailing vines. Planted islands hold narrow midnight-teal cypresses, broad verdigris leaves with coral veins, ochre cattails, white daisies and coral star flowers; olive lily pads and cream-coral lotus blossoms lie in the canals. Crisp dark ink contours, fine crosshatching and dense stippling, midnight teal, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance with parchment-colored limestone and restrained coral accents, soft upper-left illumination and consistent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the western golden route, the northern open canals and planted edges while keeping this bell pavilion and suspended droplet unique.

tiles.title: The Sixfold Rill
tiles.description: A carved limestone water-comb pours six bright arcing streams into a long teal trough among flowering canal islands and winding golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,3), directly north of The Dewbell Court and west of The Coilwell Basin. A low diagonal cream-limestone water-comb has six scalloped upright sections with leaf-like carved ornament; six blue-white arcing streams emerge from dark round openings and land in a long rounded midnight-teal trough, each with concentric pale ripple rings. Fine carved panels line the trough's outer wall, and a small cream stair sits at its lower-right side. An ochre-golden winding route reaches the left edge around half-height through a cream stair flight and continues to the top near x=0.44 with further stairs. No golden road reaches the bottom or right edge. Open teal canals and planted limestone islands continue the southern neighbor's northern edge along the bottom and the eastern neighbor's western edge along the right, with olive lily pads and cream-coral lotus blossoms; water also reaches the top and left in intervals around the road and banks. Low cream block walls and sphere-topped posts carry trailing gold-green vines. Dense islands hold narrow dark teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, broad dark leaves outlined and veined in coral, white daisies and coral star flowers. Crisp black and deep-teal ink contours, fine hatching and dense stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like limestone highlights, soft upper-left illumination, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the northern and western golden exits and the open canals; keep this six-stream scalloped trough unique.

tiles.title: Furlroot Crossing
tiles.description: A branching limestone root arches over a lotus-filled teal canal and carries a curving golden garden route.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,2), directly north of The Sixfold Rill and west of The Whisperreed Court. A broad cream-limestone root bridge curves across the center above a deep teal canal; branching stone limbs create several rounded open gaps, with delicate carved lines, hatching and trailing gold-green vines. Its ochre-orange walking surface sweeps over the upper arch and bends east, with cream stair runs and sphere-topped cream posts. Golden stair routes reach the bottom around x=0.44, the top around x=0.41, the left around mid-height, and the right slightly below mid-height. The bottom route rises through cream stairs toward a densely planted landing beside the bridge. Open teal waterways and planted cream-limestone banks continue along the bottom and right shared boundaries and in intervals along the top and left. Olive lily pads and cream-coral lotuses fill the canals; narrow midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, coral-outlined broad dark leaves, white daisies and coral star flowers crowd the islands. Low cream block walls, sphere-topped posts and gold-green hanging vines border the paths. Crisp black and deep-teal ink contours, dense stippling and fine hatching, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like masonry highlights, soft upper-left illumination and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the open canals and golden exits; keep this branching root bridge unique.

tiles.title: The Foldwater Leaf
tiles.description: An unfurled cream-limestone cascade pours through scalloped open pools beside golden stair-paths and densely planted teal canals.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,1), directly north of Furlroot Crossing and west of The Rainlace Dome. A tall cream-limestone leaflike cascade occupies the center, with three elevated open scalloped teal basins descending diagonally from upper left toward lower right into a lower circular pool. Carved curling rims, ribs, rounded openings and arched supports carry fine ochre tracery, dark ink hatching and draped gold-green vines. Blue-white waterfalls feed bright circular ripple rings in each basin and in the lower pool. A golden-orange route curves across the upper part and descends cream stairs to the right; another route crosses the lower foreground, bends into cream stairs and exits the bottom near x=0.49, rather than the requested x=0.41. The right path exits around y=0.60, below the requested connection around y=0.15 to the eastern neighbor. The top route exits near x=0.36 and the left route around y=0.60. Deep teal canals remain open beside the top and bottom routes and along intervals of both sides, between densely planted cream block banks. Olive lily pads, cream-coral lotuses, narrow midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, coral-outlined broad dark leaves, white daisies and coral star flowers fill the islets. Cream sphere-topped posts and trailing gold-green vines border the paths and banks. Crisp black and deep-teal contours, dense stippling and fine hatching, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like limestone highlights, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the canals and open golden routes; keep this open leaf cascade unique.

tiles.title: The Tidewound Gate
tiles.description: Interwoven limestone water arches rise over planted teal canals while a golden route winds beneath their blue-white falls.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,0), directly north of The Foldwater Leaf and west of The Shellspring Coil. Interwoven cream-limestone ribbon arches form an open knotted gate at the center above a branching dark-teal canal; the bands contain narrow teal runnels and are carved with fine ochre tracery, dark stippling and hatching, and draped gold-green vines. Six blue-white streams descend from the runnels and low arch openings into bright white circular ripple rings. A golden-orange walking route winds from the top near x=0.55, passes beneath the crossing arches, bends right and descends cream stairs to the bottom near x=0.54; the bottom connection is farther right than the southern neighbor's top route near x=0.36. A branch of the route crosses the left edge near y=0.53. No golden path reaches the right edge, matching the eastern neighbor's path-free western boundary. Broad teal water remains open through intervals of all four edges, including the upper and lower parts of the right boundary, beside densely planted cream block-stone banks. Olive lily pads, cream-coral lotuses, narrow midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, broad dark leaves with coral veins, white daisies and sparse coral star flowers fill the islets. Cream sphere-topped posts and trailing gold-green vines border the paths and banks. Crisp dark ink contours, dense stippling and fine hatching, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like cream limestone highlights, soft upper-left lighting and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the open canals and golden top and left routes; keep the knotted ribbon gate unique.

tiles.title: The Rainspindle Court
tiles.description: Three staggered limestone catchment dishes bloom from a twisting stem above a dark teal garden pool.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,-1), directly north of The Tidewound Gate and west of The Sieveleaf Fen. Three broad shallow cream-limestone catchment dishes on a twisting branched stem rise from a round carved pedestal in a dark-teal pool: the tallest dish opens at the upper left, the middle dish at the right, and the lowest dish at the left. Their scalloped ochre-carved rims hold teal water and trailing gold-green vines; three blue-white streams fall into bright white concentric ripple rings. A golden-orange path and cream stairs enter at the top near x=0.42, curve downward behind the landmark, and another visible golden-orange stair route enters at the bottom near x=0.56, close to the southern neighbor's top route near x=0.55. A golden-orange route crosses the left edge near y=0.49 and curves inward behind planting. No golden route reaches the right edge, matching the eastern neighbor's path-free left boundary. Broad teal canals remain open along all four edges among densely planted cream block-stone banks. Olive lily pads, cream-coral lotuses, midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, dark broad leaves with coral veins, white daisies and sparse coral star flowers cover the islets. Cream sphere-topped posts border the paths; vines trail from the banks and dishes. Crisp dark ink contours, dense stippling, fine hatching, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm cream parchment-like limestone highlights, soft upper-left illumination and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the top and left routes and open canals; keep the three-dish rain spindle unique.

tiles.title: The Rillharp Grove
tiles.description: Five hanging limestone chimes pour luminous rills beneath a carved crescent arbor amid the branching canals of a densely planted garden.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,-2), directly north of The Rainspindle Court and west of The Dewvault Cradle. A tall asymmetric cream-limestone crescent arbor rises on a carved round right-hand pedestal beside a shallow semicircular stepped pool. Five decorated tubular stone chimes of unequal lengths hang from its curved upper beam, each releasing a blue-white stream into a separate white concentric ripple ring. Ochre-green vines trail from the arch and among the chimes. A golden-orange path and cream stairs enter at the top near x=0.44, curve behind the arbor, and reappear below its semicircular steps to reach the bottom near x=0.52; this bottom entrance lies slightly east of the southern neighbor's top route near x=0.42. A golden-orange left branch enters near y=0.49 and curves diagonally toward the lower path. No golden route reaches the right edge, preserving the eastern neighbor's canal-and-island boundary. Deep teal waterways continue along all four edges between densely planted cream block-stone banks; small bank waterfalls appear near the lower left and along the right edge. Olive lily pads, cream-coral lotuses, slim midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, white daisies, dark broad coral-veined leaves and sparse coral star flowers fill the islets. Cream sphere-topped posts line the golden paths. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and dense stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm cream parchment-like limestone highlights, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the upper and left golden routes and open canals; keep the five-chime crescent arbor unique.

tiles.title: The Seedcrown Cistern
tiles.description: A carved lotus-shaped limestone bowl releases five slender streams into a round stepped basin amid dense canal gardens and branching golden walks.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,-3), directly north of The Rillharp Grove and west of The Rainharp Court. A large carved cream-limestone lotus-shaped bowl with curled and pointed petal rims is raised above a low round stepped teal basin. Olive lily pads and one cream-coral lotus float in the upper bowl; five blue-white streams descend from its underside into five separate white concentric ripple rings below. Ochre-green vines drape from the petal rims and round basin walls. A golden-orange route enters the top near x=0.36 through cream stairs, curves down-right behind the bowl, and reappears around the left and bottom of the basin before reaching the bottom near x=0.53 through another stair flight. This bottom entrance is slightly east of the southern reference's top entrance near x=0.44. A gold branch reaches the left edge near y=0.48. No golden path reaches the right edge, which preserves the eastern neighbor's open canal-and-island boundary. Deep teal channels and densely planted cream block-stone banks continue at all four edges; small white bank waterfalls create ripple rings near the upper left, lower left, upper right and middle right. Olive lily pads, coral-edged cream lotus flowers, slim midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, white daisylike flowers, large dark coral-veined leaves and sparse coral star flowers fill the islets. Cream sphere-topped posts line the paths and central basin. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and dense stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like cream limestone highlights, soft upper-left lighting, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the northern and western golden routes and open waterways; keep the lotus water bowl unique.

tiles.title: The Seedveil Arbor
tiles.description: Two tall limestone seed-husk wings cradle a vine lattice of suspended ochre seeds above a golden garden path.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,-4), directly north of The Seedcrown Cistern and west of The Fernfold Terrace. Two tall cream-limestone seed-husk sides curve inward to pointed tips, forming an airy vertical oval arbor around a midnight-teal interlaced vine lattice hung with numerous pale ochre seed beads. Ochre-green vines drape down the outer masonry, while reeds and white daisylike flowers fill planted cream block-stone banks around the open golden route beneath it. The golden-orange path enters the bottom through cream stairs near x=0.47, curves upward through the arbor, and exits the top through stairs near x=0.59. The bottom entrance lies east of the southern reference's top entrance near x=0.36. A gold branch reaches the left edge near y=0.50; no golden path reaches the right edge. Deep teal branching canals and densely planted cream-limestone banks remain open at all four edges, with olive lily pads, pale bubble clusters, cream-coral lotus flowers, and white ripple rings beneath small bank waterfalls at upper left, lower left and two positions along the right. Slim midnight-teal cypresses, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, white flowers, dark coral-veined leaves and coral star flowers fill the islands. Cream sphere-topped posts line the golden routes and arbor; square cream pillars punctuate the planted banks. Detailed dark ink contours, fine hatching and dense stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like cream limestone highlights, soft upper-left illumination, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the actual northern and western golden exits and open waterways while keeping this seed-husk arbor unique.

tiles.title: The Upflow Spring
tiles.description: An intertwined ribbon of water rises from a stepped limestone basin among planted canals and branching golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,-5), directly north of The Seedveil Arbor and west of The Seedbell Basin. A round cream-limestone basin with a thick block-stone rim and short stairs facing downward occupies the central garden island. Two slender teal water ribbons rise from the basin, cross and loop together overhead before returning to the water, with several pale hanging droplets and small ripples around their feet. Dark slender cypresses, white daisylike flowers and tiny blooms, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails and hanging vines, coral star flowers and dark coral-veined leaves densely plant the island and surrounding cream block retaining banks. The golden-orange route enters the bottom through cream stairs near x=0.52, curls right of the central island, then continues upward behind the basin to the top near x=0.40 through another cream stair flight. Its actual bottom entrance lies west of the southern reference's top exit near x=0.59. A connected golden branch curves around the island's lower-left side and crosses a small cream bridge toward the left edge near y=0.50. No golden route reaches the right edge, consistent with the eastern reference's left edge. Cream sphere-topped posts mark the stairs and golden routes; small square cream pillars punctuate the planted banks. Deep teal and verdigris canals with olive lily pads, pale bubble clusters, coral-edged cream lotus blooms and fine ripples remain open at all four edges. Two small cream-bank waterfalls at upper right and lower right spill into white concentric ripple rings. Dense dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like limestone highlights, restrained coral, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the actual northern and western golden exits and open waterways while keeping this looping upflow spring unique.

tiles.title: The Tideglass Grove
tiles.description: A curling teal tree carries glasslike seed pods filled with tiny rippling pools above a densely planted limestone garden island.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-6,-6), directly north of The Upflow Spring. A curved dark teal tree with branching leafy arms stands in the central cream-block retaining island; several large transparent teardrop-shaped seed pods hang from its branches, each visibly holding a tiny level pool with pale concentric ripples, with smaller droplet pods among the leaves. Dark slender cypresses, white daisylike flowers, verdigris reeds, ochre cattails, coral star flowers and dark coral-veined leaves densely fill the central and surrounding islands. The orange-gold route enters the bottom near x=0.50 through cream steps and sphere-topped posts, bends around the right side of the tree island, then continues behind it to the top near x=0.53 through another cream stair flight. Its actual bottom entrance lies east of the southern reference's top exit near x=0.40. A connected golden branch crosses a short curved cream bridge and leaves the right edge near y=0.45; no golden path reaches the left edge. A small stair flight leads from the path into the central grove at its lower side. Deep teal and verdigris canals with olive lily pads, pale bubble clusters, coral-edged cream lotus blooms and fine ripples remain open at all four edges. Cream pillar-bank waterfalls at the left-middle, upper-right and lower-right fall into bright pale ripple rings. Cream sphere-topped posts and small square pillars mark paths and planting banks. Dense dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like limestone highlights, restrained coral, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the actual northern and eastern golden exits and open waterways while keeping the water-bearing glass seed tree unique.

tiles.title: The Ripple Loom
tiles.description: A cream stone water harp pours slender streams into a rippling pool amid lush canal gardens crossed by a golden path.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-5,-6), directly east of The Tideglass Grove and north of The Seedbell Basin. Five curved cream-limestone ribs with sphere-topped ends form an open harp pavilion on the central retaining island; thin pale blue vertical streams descend from the ribs into a dark teal circular collecting pool with several pale concentric ripple rings. A short cream stair flight leads up into the pool pavilion from its lower side. Dense slender dark cypresses, white daisylike blooms, verdigris and ochre reeds, coral starflowers and coral-veined dark leaves plant the central and surrounding islands; cream stippled block pillars and low retaining banks border them. The orange-gold path enters the left edge near y=0.48 through a cream arched bridge with sphere-topped posts, curves around the lower side of the central island, and crosses a matching bridge before leaving the right edge near y=0.49. Its actual left entrance sits slightly below the western reference's right exit near y=0.45. No golden route reaches the top or bottom edge. Deep teal and verdigris canals, olive round lily pads, pale clustered ripples and coral-edged cream lotus blooms remain open at all four edges. The southern edge continues the northern waterways and planted bank fragments of The Seedbell Basin. Cream pillar waterfalls at upper-right and lower-right descend into bright pale ripple rings. Dense dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like cream limestone, restrained coral accents, soft upper-left light, and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the actual eastern golden exit and open northern waterways while keeping this five-stream water harp unique.

tiles.title: The Waking Husk
tiles.description: An etched limestone seed husk encloses a curled blue spring above a lily-filled pool beside the continuing golden garden path.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-4,-6), directly east of The Ripple Loom and north of The Turning Rill. A tall cream-limestone seed-husk sculpture of several asymmetric tapered curved lobes, etched with fine dots and oval ring marks, rises from a dark teal circular pool enclosed by a low cream block retaining wall. A slender pale blue stream descends from the inward curl of the tallest upper lobe into bright concentric ripples at the pool center; olive lily pads sit in the pool. A short cream stair flight leads down from the pool's near side to the orange-gold route. The route enters the left edge near y=0.49 through a cream arched bridge with sphere-topped posts, curves around the lower side of the central planted island, and crosses a matching bridge before leaving the right edge near y=0.47. No golden path reaches the top or bottom. The bottom continues the open teal water and planted bank fragments of The Turning Rill's top edge. Branching midnight-teal and verdigris waterways remain open at all four edges around irregular islands with slender dark cypresses, white daisylike flowers, ochre and verdigris reeds, coral starflowers and broad dark coral-veined leaves. Cream stippled square posts border banks. Olive circular lily pads, pale clustered ripples and coral-edged cream lotus blooms occupy the canals. Cream pillar waterfalls at the upper-right and lower-right fall into pale circular ripple rings. Dense dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like cream limestone highlights, restrained coral accents, soft upper-left light, and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the actual eastern golden exit and open northern waterways while keeping this curled seed-husk spring unique.

tiles.title: The Rain Harp
tiles.description: A curved limestone lintel pours a row of delicate water strings into an island pool where golden paths meet among teal canals and flowering banks.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-3,-6), directly east of The Waking Husk and north of The Dew Ladder. A broad cream-limestone lintel curves gently upward at both ends and rests on two tapered pylons etched with dotted lines and oval ring marks. A row of thin pale-blue water streams descends from its underside into bright small ripple circles within a midnight-teal oval pool; olive lily pads sit around the streams. A low segmented cream block wall borders the pool, and a short cream stair flight descends from the near side toward the orange-gold route. The route enters the left edge near y=0.47 through a cream arched bridge with sphere-topped posts, curves around the lower central planted island, crosses a matching bridge and leaves the right edge near y=0.47. A branch curves downward through a short stair flight and exits the bottom near x=0.63, connecting toward The Dew Ladder's top route near x=0.60. No golden route reaches the top. Branching midnight-teal and verdigris waterways remain open at all four edges, around irregular planted banks and islands with slender dark cypresses, white daisylike flowers, ochre and verdigris reeds, coral starflowers and broad dark coral-veined leaves. Stippled square cream posts border banks; olive circular lily pads, pale clustered ripples and coral-edged cream lotus blooms occupy the canals. Cream pillar waterfalls at the upper-right and lower-right fall into pale concentric ripple rings. Dense dark ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance, warm parchment-like cream limestone highlights, restrained coral accents, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the actual open northern and eastern waterways and eastern golden exit while keeping this water harp unique.

tiles.title: The Tide Cup
tiles.description: A fluted limestone cup pours two streams into a lily-filled pool above branching stone roots and a curving golden route.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-2,-6), directly east of The Rain Harp and north of The Hollow Seed. A wide shallow fluted cream-limestone bowl tilts above a midnight-teal oval pool on cream branching rootlike supports. The open oval bowl contains dark teal water traced with pale concentric and swirling lines. Two pale turquoise-white streams spill from the left and right low rim into separate concentric ripple patches below; ochre vines trail from the right rim and among the supports. A low segmented cream block wall with several sphere-topped pillars borders the pool, and a short cream stair flight descends from its near side to the orange-gold route. The route enters the left edge near y=0.48 through a cream arched bridge with sphere-topped posts, curves around the near bank, crosses a matching bridge and exits the right edge near y=0.52. A branch descends through another short cream stair flight and exits the bottom near x=0.58, slightly left of The Hollow Seed's top entrance near x=0.63. No golden route reaches the top. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals remain open across all four edges, around irregular planted banks and islands with slender dark cypresses, white daisylike flowers, ochre and verdigris reeds, coral starflowers, dark coral-veined broad leaves and square cream posts. tiles.title: The Unfurling Spring

tiles.description: A curled ivory fern lattice carries luminous turquoise water above a teal canal between flowering banks and golden bridge paths.

A tall warm-ivory limestone fern lattice rises from a low engraved round base in the central pool, curves left and upward, and curls inward on the upper right. Open branching ribs surround turquoise water ribbons; ochre botanical engravings decorate the broad lower stem and base, and hanging golden vines flank the lattice. A bright white-turquoise stream falls from the inner curl into pale dotted concentric ripples to the right of the base, with further concentric ripples around the base. An orange-gold route enters the top near x=0.53, descends short cream stairs between sphere-topped ivory piers and ends as a straight promontory above the lattice; it is visibly separate from the lower route. A golden-orange route enters the left near y=0.50 over a low ivory arched bridge with round-finial piers, sweeps around the lower side of the pool and rises to a matching bridge exiting the right near y=0.50. Its lower-middle branch descends cream stairs and exits the bottom near x=0.58. Open midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach all four edges around curving ivory-edged planted banks. Four small corner-bank waterfalls pour into luminous dotted rings. Slender ink-dark cypresses, large dark leaves with coral veins, ochre seedheads and trailing vines, white daisylike and drooping flowers, coral starflowers and engraved ivory posts cover the banks. Olive segmented lily pads, circular pale netlike pad clusters and glowing cream/coral lotus blooms float in the canals. Dense dark ink contours, fine hatching and ochre stippling, midnight-teal/verdigris watercolor, warm parchment-like cream masonry and orange-ochre paths with restrained coral; upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the northern stair entrance, western and eastern bridge routes, southern stair exit and open canals while keeping the curled fern lattice unique.

tiles.title: The Rainseed Lantern
tiles.description: A pierced ivory seedpod lantern cradles a luminous turquoise water orb above a rippling canal garden.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,-4), below The Fernwater Filigree and east of The Tideweaver Crossing. A large upright warm-ivory limestone seedpod lantern stands on a short engraved circular plinth in the central pool, with broad curved ribs, tall oval openings, a small round finial, ochre and coral botanical engravings and long hanging gold vines. A luminous turquoise orb floats inside; a bright white-turquoise stream falls from its underside through the lower opening into pale dotted concentric ripples below and around the base. A golden-orange route enters the top near x=0.53, descends cream steps between sphere-topped ivory piers and bends toward the upper-right planted bank, visibly separate from the lower route. A golden-orange route enters the left near y=0.50 over a low ivory arched bridge, sweeps below the central pool and rises to a matching bridge exiting the right near y=0.50. Its lower-middle branch descends cream stairs and exits the bottom near x=0.58. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach all four edges around irregular ivory-edged planted banks; small waterfalls pour from all four corner banks into luminous dotted ripples. Slender ink-dark cypresses, large coral-veined dark leaves, ochre seedheads and trailing gold vines, white daisylike flowers, coral starflowers and round-finial ivory posts cover the banks. Olive segmented lily pads, pale circular netlike pad clusters and cream-coral lotus flowers float in the open water. Dense dark ink contours, fine hatching and ochre stippling, translucent midnight-teal/verdigris watercolor, parchment-ivory masonry and orange-ochre paths with restrained coral; upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the top stair entrance, western and eastern bridge routes, southern stair exit and edge canals while keeping the rainseed lantern unique.

tiles.title: The Dewharp Grove
tiles.description: A curling ivory water harp suspends turquoise droplets and delicate falls above a canal garden threaded with golden paths.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,-3), below The Rainseed Lantern and east of The Quietcoil Cistern. A large warm-ivory limestone water harp stands in the central teal pool: two outward-curling broad uprights bear coral-ochre botanical engravings and meet a curved crosspiece, with long gold vines hanging from the top and crescent base. Fine vertical gold strands hold turquoise droplets, and several luminous white-turquoise rivulets descend into pale dotted concentric ripples under and around the harp. A golden-orange route enters the top near x=0.58, descends cream steps between round-finial ivory posts and bends across the upper-right bank to exit the right near y=0.42. A separate route enters the left over a low ivory arched bridge near y=0.46, curves through the lower-left bank, crosses a second ivory arched bridge in the lower middle and descends cream steps to exit the bottom near x=0.56. The western route entrance is visibly higher than the western neighbor's supplied exit. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach portions of all four edges around irregular ivory-edged planted banks. Small bank waterfalls appear near upper-left, lower-left and lower-right. Slender ink-dark cypresses, large coral-veined dark leaves, white daisylike and drooping flowers, coral starflowers, ochre seedheads, trailing gold vines and round-finial ivory posts fill the banks. Olive segmented lily pads, pale circular netlike pad clusters and cream-coral lotus flowers float in the water. Dense dark contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent teal/verdigris watercolor appearance, parchment-ivory masonry and orange-ochre paths with restrained coral; upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue top stairs, west bridge entrance, eastern route and south stair exit plus edge canals; keep the water harp unique.

tiles.title: The Pearlwake Grotto
tiles.description: An engraved ivory spiral shell shelters a stepped pool and pours three slender waterfalls into a garden canal.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,-2), below The Dewharp Grove and east of The Glassreed Arcade. A large warm-ivory spiral shell grotto occupies the central canal: a tight curl on its left and a broad open mouth on its right carry coral-ochre leaf and flower engravings, with golden vines and white daisies hanging from the ridges. The shaded inner chamber contains pale slender supports and a small teal pool bordered by curved descending ivory steps. Three narrow luminous white-turquoise falls descend from the grotto into pale dotted concentric ripples. A golden-orange route enters the top near x=0.57 on ivory stairs between round-finial posts, curves behind the upper grotto bank and exits the right near y=0.43. Another route enters the left over a low ivory arched bridge near y=0.47 and bends toward the grotto's left bank; this western entrance is visibly above the western neighbor's supplied exit near y=0.58. A separate low ivory arched bridge in the lower center leads onto cream stairs and an orange route exiting the bottom near x=0.62. Midnight-teal and verdigris water reaches portions of all four edges, with olive segmented lily pads, cream coral-edged lotus blooms and pale circular netlike pad clusters. Small white bank falls occur near upper-left, lower-left and lower-right. Irregular dark planted banks edged with ivory scalloped masonry and some rough stones hold slender cypresses, large coral-veined leaves, coral starflowers, white daisies and drooping flowers, ochre seedheads and golden trailing vines. Dense black and deep-teal contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent teal-verdigris watercolor appearance, warm parchment-ivory limestone, orange-ochre paths and restrained coral; upper-left illumination and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the top stairs, west bridge entrance, eastern route and south stair exit plus edge canals; keep this spiral shell grotto unique.

tiles.title: The Rainbowl Arbor
tiles.description: An engraved ivory tree holds four teal rain basins that cascade through a lush canal garden crossed by golden paths and a low arched bridge.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,-1), below The Pearlwake Grotto and east of The Ivory Tidewheel. A tall asymmetrical warm-ivory branching tree rises from a low central planted island; its four shallow bowls hold teal water, with the broadest crescent bowl high on the left, a small bowl on a short left arm, a broad middle bowl on the right, and a smaller low-right bowl. Coral-ochre leaf engravings run along the trunk, branches and bowl rims; golden vines and white daisies drape the crown and arms. Four slender luminous white-turquoise falls connect the top bowl to the middle-right bowl, the middle-right bowl to the lower-right bowl, and the small-left and lower-right bowls to pale dotted concentric canal ripples. The golden-orange path enters the top on ivory stairs near x=0.60, descends behind the bowls and bends to exit the right near y=0.44. Another orange route enters the left near y=0.46, crosses a low ivory arched footbridge with round-finial posts around (0.24,0.55), and reaches the tree island; this western entry is visibly above the supplied western neighbor's exit near y=0.64. An orange route from the lower island runs between posts onto ivory stairs exiting the bottom near x=0.60. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach portions of all four edges, with olive segmented lily pads, cream coral-edged lotus flowers and pale round netlike pad clusters. Small white bank falls appear at the upper-left and lower-right. Irregular dark planted banks carry ivory scalloped rims and some rough stones, slender cypresses, large coral-veined leaves, coral starflowers, white daisies and drooping white blooms, ochre seedheads and golden trailing vines. Dense black and deep-teal contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent teal-verdigris watercolor appearance, warm parchment-ivory stone, orange-ochre routes and restrained coral; upper-left illumination and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the north stair, west bridge route, east path and south stairs plus edge canals; keep this branching four-basin arbor unique.

tiles.title: The Shellsong Sluice
tiles.description: An engraved ivory coiled shell gathers teal water in nested chambers and sends slender falls into a lily-filled canal beside golden garden stairs.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,0), below The Rainbowl Arbor and east of The Rainstring Arbor. A large upright open warm-ivory coiled shell occupies the central planted island; coral-ochre botanical engravings trace its ridges, and teal water fills several nested scalloped chambers. Thin luminous white-turquoise falls drop between the inner chambers and from the lower-right shell lip to pale concentric canal ripples. Golden vines and white daisies drape the shell. The golden-orange route enters the top on ivory steps near x=0.60, descends behind the shell and reaches the island. A golden-orange route enters the left near y=0.68, crosses a low ivory arched footbridge with round-finial posts around (0.27,0.56), and reaches the shell island; this is slightly lower at the boundary than the supplied western neighbor's exit near y=0.66. A route exits the right near y=0.54, and ivory stairs leave the bottom near x=0.58. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach portions of all four edges, carrying olive segmented lily pads, cream lotus blossoms edged in coral and pale round coral-dotted netlike discs. Small white bank falls appear at the upper-left and lower-right. Dark irregular planted banks with rough ivory stones and scalloped edging carry slender cypresses, coral-veined teal leaves, coral stars, white daisies and drooping blooms, ochre seedheads and golden trailing vines. Dense black/deep-teal contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent teal-verdigris watercolor appearance, warm parchment-ivory shell and stone, orange-ochre routes and restrained coral, upper-left light, coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the north stair, west bridge route, east path, south stairs and edge canals; keep this coiled shell sluice unique.

tiles.title: The Ginkgo Rainfan
tiles.description: An ivory ginkgo fan channels teal water through branching veins and spills slender cascades into its flower-lined island canals.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,1), below The Shellsong Sluice and east of The Spiralwell Garden. A large upright warm-ivory ginkgo fan occupies center-right on a slim branching limestone pedestal rooted in a small planted island; its broad radial lobes carry orange-ochre ginkgo engravings, while teal water channels follow several spreading veins. Thin white-turquoise cascades spill from the left lower fan tip, a left-center vein, an inner right lobe and the far-right tip to pale concentric canal ripples. Gold-green vines and white daisies drape the upper fan lobes and parts of the pedestal. A golden-orange ivory stair route enters the top near x=0.60, descends behind the fan and reaches the island; this is slightly right of the supplied northern neighbor's bottom exit near x=0.58. A golden-orange route enters the left near y=0.66 and crosses a low ivory arched footbridge with round-finial posts near (0.30,0.52) toward the island. Another path exits the right near y=0.54, and the island's ivory stair route exits the bottom near x=0.58. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach portions of all four edges, carrying olive segmented lily pads, cream lotus blossoms edged in coral, and pale round coral-dotted discs. Small bank falls appear at the upper-left and lower-right. Irregular warm-ivory stone banks with scalloped edging and cream round-finial posts bear slender deep-teal cypresses, large coral-veined teal leaves, coral stars, white daisies and drooping blooms, ochre seedheads and gold-green trailing vines. Dense black/deep-teal ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent teal-verdigris watercolor appearance on warm parchment, ivory stone, orange-ochre routes and restrained coral; upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the north stair route, west bridge route, east path, south stairs and edge canals; keep this ginkgo fan sluice unique.

tiles.title: The Starpod Cistern
tiles.description: An ivory poppy seedpod cistern spills four narrow cascades from its shoulders beneath an open star-shaped teal crown basin.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,2), below The Ginkgo Rainfan and east of The Veinleaf Aqueduct. A large rounded upright warm-ivory limestone poppy seedpod cistern stands at center-right on slender branching arched supports rooted beside the island stairs. Its ribbed body carries orange-ochre engraved poppy pods, stems, leaves and dotted ornament. Its scalloped star-shaped crown is an open dark-teal basin with pale ripples; four pale blue-white shoulder cascades fall around the body to concentric canal ripples, while additional round shoulder apertures remain dry. Gold-green vines and white daisies drape the crown, body and supports. A golden-orange ivory stair route enters the top near x=0.61, continues behind the cistern, and emerges beneath its supports into island stairs exiting the bottom near x=0.59. A golden-orange path enters the left near y=0.67 and crosses a low ivory arched bridge with round-finial posts near (0.32,0.51), with its connection toward the island screened by growth. Another golden-orange route exits the right near y=0.54. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach portions of every edge, carrying segmented olive lily pads, cream lotus blossoms edged with coral, and small pale coral-dotted discs. Ivory bank spouts at upper-left and lower-right make additional narrow falls. Irregular ivory stone banks and round-finial posts carry slender deep-teal cypresses, large coral-veined teal leaves, coral stars, white daisies and dense gold-green hanging vines. Dense black/deep-teal ink contours, fine hatching and stippling with teal-verdigris watercolor appearance on warm parchment, ivory stone and orange-ochre routes; restrained coral accents, upper-left lighting and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the top and bottom stairs, west bridge route, east path and open edge canals; keep this star-crowned poppy seedpod cistern unique.

tiles.title: The Moonfern Weir
tiles.description: A curled ivory stone fern channels teal water through its tapering leaflets above a garden stairway and lotus-filled canals.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,3), below The Starpod Cistern and east of The Bellwater Bower. A tall warm-ivory limestone fern aqueduct occupies center-right, with a curled spiral tip holding dark-teal water and alternating elongated pointed leaflets shaped as shallow teal-water troughs. Orange-ochre engraved fern sprigs and dotted ornament cover its stem, curl and leaflets. Narrow pale blue-white cascades descend between several troughs and into concentric canal ripples. The curved stem and branching pointed stone arches straddle the island stairway; gold-green hanging vines and white daisies drape the basins and supports. Golden-orange stairs enter the top near x=0.61, descend diagonally through left-center, continue below the fern arches and exit the bottom near x=0.56. A golden-orange route enters the left around y=0.55, crosses a low ivory arched bridge with round-finial posts near (0.32,0.55), and joins the stairs. Another golden route exits the right around y=0.51, with its interior connection screened by planting. Midnight-teal and verdigris canals reach portions of every edge, carrying segmented olive lily pads, cream coral-edged lotuses and pale circular coral-dotted discs. Small ivory bank spouts at upper-left, lower-left and lower-right send falls into pale rings. Dense planted ivory banks and round-finial posts carry slender dark-teal cypresses, broad coral-veined teal leaves, coral stars, white daisies and gold-green trailing growth. Detailed black and deep-teal ink contours, hatching and dense stippling with teal-verdigris and orange-ochre watercolor appearance on warm parchment ivory stone, restrained coral accents, upper-left lighting and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the top and bottom stairs, west bridge route, east path and open canals; keep this curled limestone fern aqueduct unique.

tiles.title: The Honeyvault Wells
tiles.description: Seven joined hexagonal limestone wells lift teal water over a canal garden, spilling pale cascades beside a golden stair and ivory footbridge.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,4), below The Moonfern Weir and east of The Threadroot Arcade. Center-right contains seven broad open hexagonal warm-ivory limestone water cups in a honeycomb cluster, with a central cup and six surrounding cups stepped at different heights. Deep-teal water fills the cups; narrow carved stone connectors and pale blue-white spillways join them. Orange-ochre honeycomb motifs and flowering sprigs decorate the faceted cup walls. Pointed arch openings pierce the supporting stone below, and several pale cascades descend from the lower cup edges into concentric canal ripples. Gold-green hanging vines and white daisies drape several rims and supports. A golden-orange stair enters the top around x=0.59, descends diagonally through left-center, then bends toward lower-center and exits the bottom around x=0.59. A golden route enters the left around y=0.60, crosses a shallow ivory arched bridge with round-finial posts near (0.28,0.55), and joins the stair near (0.38,0.58). A separate visible golden route exits the right around y=0.51 with its interior connection screened by planting. Midnight-teal and verdigris canal water reaches portions of every edge around planted banks, with segmented olive lily pads, cream coral-edged lotuses and pale scalloped coral-dotted discs. Small ivory bank spouts at upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right spill into pale circular ripples. Warm-ivory banks and round-finial posts carry slender dark-teal cypresses, broad coral-veined leaves, white daisies, coral star flowers and fine gold-green growth. Detailed black and deep-teal ink contours, fine hatching and dense stippling with midnight-teal, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance on warm parchment ivory stone, restrained coral accents, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the top and bottom stair, west bridge route, east path and open canals; keep these honeycomb wells unique.

tiles.title: The Coilsong Cistern
tiles.description: An engraved ivory spiral cistern carries teal water through a coiled channel and spills three luminous falls into the surrounding garden canals.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,5), below The Honeyvault Wells and east of The Fanleaf Rills. Center-right holds one broad raised circular ivory limestone cistern whose continuous open teal channel coils inward to a round central pool. Orange-ochre leafy engravings cover the wide spiral rim, smaller carved motifs cover its vertical walls, and a small honeycomb ornament appears on the lower front wall. Three pale blue-white spillways descend from its lower-left, lower-middle and right sides into concentric pale canal ripples. Gold-green trailing vines and white daisies drape its rims. Golden-orange stairs enter the top near x=0.55, descend diagonally through left-center, bend below the cistern, and exit the bottom near x=0.60. A golden route enters the left near y=0.62, crosses a shallow ivory arched bridge with round-finial posts near (0.27,0.55), and joins the stairs near (0.38,0.58). A separate golden route exits the right near y=0.51, with its inward connection screened by planting. Midnight-teal and verdigris canal water reaches portions of all four boundaries around ivory planted banks. Segmented olive lily pads, cream coral-edged lotuses and pale scalloped coral-dotted discs occupy the water. Small ivory spouts near the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right edges spill into pale circular ripples. Round-finial ivory posts, slender dark-teal cypresses, broad coral-veined leaves, white daisies, coral star flowers and fine gold-green growth surround the waterways. Detailed black and deep-teal ink contours, dense stippling and fine hatching with midnight-teal, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance on warm parchment ivory limestone, restrained coral accents, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the north and south stairs, west bridge route, east path and open canals; keep this coiled cistern unique.

tiles.title: The Veinwater Aqueduct
tiles.description: A raised carved limestone leaf carries branching teal rills above the garden canals and spills two bright waterfalls beside the golden stairs.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,6), below The Coilsong Cistern and east of The Droplet Sanctuary. A broad raised ivory limestone leaf aqueduct extends diagonally from a pointed upper-left tip near (0.34,0.22) to its lower-right stem near (0.73,0.63). A continuous dark-teal central vein and curved branching open channels divide its ochre leaf-engraved ivory surface. Short carved supports are visible beneath the lower edge. Two pale blue-white waterfalls descend from that edge near x=0.56 and x=0.74 into pale concentric ripples in the surrounding canal. Gold-green vines and white daisies drape the aqueduct rim. Golden-orange stairs enter the top near x=0.55, run downward behind the leaf, reappear below its right side near (0.62,0.74), and curve to a bottom exit near x=0.56. A golden route enters the left near y=0.61 and crosses a shallow ivory arched bridge with round-finial posts near (0.28,0.55) toward the aqueduct; its inward junction is screened by planting and the raised leaf. A separate small golden path fragment touches the right edge near y=0.54, with its inner connection hidden by plants. Midnight-teal and verdigris canal water reaches portions of every boundary between ivory planted banks. Segmented olive lily pads, cream coral-edged lotuses and pale scalloped discs with coral dots float in the canals. Small ivory bank spouts at the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right spill into pale ripples. Round-finial ivory posts, slender dark-teal cypresses, broad coral-veined leaves, white daisies, sparse coral star flowers and fine gold-green growth repeat around the waterways. Detailed black and deep-teal ink contours, dense stippling and fine hatching with midnight-teal, verdigris and ochre watercolor appearance on warm parchment ivory limestone, restrained coral accents, soft upper-left light and coherent high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the north and south stairs, west bridge route, east path fragment and open canals; keep this branching leaf aqueduct unique.

tiles.title: The Whorlshell Reservoir
tiles.description: An ivory spiral-shell reservoir winds teal water above the canals and releases a single cascade beside golden garden stairs.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,7), below The Veinwater Aqueduct and east of The Pearlroot Basins. A broad raised ivory limestone shell reservoir occupies the center, from approximately (0.34,0.27) to (0.70,0.60), with curved ochre-engraved partitions enclosing a continuous teal spiral channel that coils inward near (0.53,0.45). A rounded ridged shell wall rises along the right rim. One pale blue-white cascade descends from the lower-right lip near (0.62,0.56) to concentric ripple rings in the surrounding canal near (0.63,0.63). Golden-orange stairs enter the top near x=0.55, descend diagonally along the reservoir's upper-right side and disappear into planting, then reappear below near (0.60,0.67) and bend toward a bottom exit near x=0.55. A shallow ivory arched bridge with ochre joints crosses the left-side canal around (0.18,0.46); its outer route is screened by the planted left bank and its inner end by the reservoir-side growth. A separate golden path fragment touches the right edge near y=0.47, screened inward by planting. Midnight-teal and verdigris canal water reaches portions of all four edges between planted ivory banks. Segmented olive lily pads, cream coral-edged lotuses, and pale scalloped discs with coral dots float in the canals. Small ivory bank spouts near the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right spill into concentric ripples. Round-finial ivory posts, narrow dark-teal cypresses, broad coral-veined leaves, white daisies, sparse coral star flowers and dense trailing gold-green vines repeat around the waterways. Detailed black and deep-teal ink contours, fine hatching and stippling, translucent watercolor appearance on warm parchment ivory stone with midnight teal, verdigris and ochre, restrained coral accents, soft upper-left light, high bird's-eye/isometric miniature-garden scale. Continue the top and bottom golden stairs, the right-edge path fragment, the screened left bridge route and open canals; keep this spiral-shell reservoir unique.

tiles.title: The Rainleaf Arboretum
tiles.description: An ivory branching leaf fountain gathers teal water in engraved cups above a planted canal island, while a small hovering cup pours into the basin beneath it.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (8,8), directly below The Whorlshell Reservoir. A branching ivory limestone leaf fountain occupies the central round planted island: two broad ochre-veined cupped leaves rise on curving forked stems from approximately (0.33,0.31) to (0.69,0.55), holding teal water. Pale blue-white falls descend from the outer lips into concentric canal ripples at approximately (0.37,0.49) and (0.68,0.47). A smaller ivory leaf cup hovers above the right basin near (0.64,0.26), joined to its water by a narrow vertical falling stream. The island has an engraved low ivory circular wall, dense trailing gold-green vines, white daisies, coral stars, dark-teal cypresses and large coral-veined leaves. Golden stairs enter the top near x=0.53 and approach the island behind the fountain; another stair route emerges from its lower side, crosses an ivory arched footbridge near (0.46,0.74), then runs to the bottom near x=0.45. A separate golden route from a short exposed segment southeast of the island crosses the right edge near y=0.77, screened at its inner end by planting. Midnight-teal and verdigris canal water reaches portions of all four edges between heavily planted banks. Segmented olive lily pads, cream coral-edged lotuses and cream scalloped discs dotted coral float on the water. Multiple round-finial ivory bank spouts pour pale falls into ringed ripples. Crisp black and deep-teal contours, fine hatching and stippling, watercolor-like washes on warm ivory parchment stone, midnight teal, verdigris and ochre with restrained coral, soft upper-left light, high bird's-eye/isometric miniature garden scale. Continue the top/bottom golden routes, the screened right-side route and open canals; preserve the branching leaf fountain and hovering cup as this region's unique landmark.

tiles.title: The Loopwater Knot
tiles.description: An interlaced ivory ribbon crossing curls around twin teal pools above a planted canal island, with a pale waterfall and a golden stair route along its western bank.
tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (7,8), directly below The Pearlroot Basins and left of The Rainleaf Arboretum. An engraved ivory limestone ribbon forms a central looping crossing around two rounded teal-water pools, with ochre walking surfaces and low ivory parapets. The upper loop curls from approximately (0.46,0.30) around (0.63,0.36), crosses diagonally toward the lower left, and passes behind the broad foreground ribbon that runs from about (0.30,0.56) to (0.69,0.57). The left pool is near (0.46,0.45); the right pool is near (0.64,0.51). A blue-white waterfall spills from the front lip of the right pool near x=0.66 into concentric pale ripple rings near (0.66,0.66). The central crossing rises from a dense planted bank with a branching ivory support, trailing gold-green vines, white daisies, coral stars, dark-teal cypresses and broad coral-veined leaves. A separate golden stair route enters the left edge near y=0.46, descends diagonally along the western bank and exits the bottom near x=0.30. The short lower-left stair of the central crossing ends within planting; no clear connection to that separate western route is exposed. Midnight-teal and verdigris open canal water reaches portions of all four edges between heavily planted banks. tiles.title: The Rainstring Cloister

tiles.continuity: Single full-bleed square at (-8,1), directly north of The Rainfern Terrace and west of The Coilseed Spring.
